 Final Table: 5 twists that let Famiglia turn Pyeongyeon’s tournament against it
 Pyeongyeon wants the tournament to move past the crisis. Song-yi realizes she can enter it and turn that strategy against the group.
 By Jeff Souza • @papodedorama @papodedorama • Published on 25.10.2026 at 16:46 
 Image for Final Table: 5 twists that let Famiglia turn Pyeongyeon’s tournament against it.

 Español Pyeongyeon Group sees its cooking tournament as a way out of the Famiglia crisis, but Episode 2 of Final Table starts turning that strategy against the company itself. Song-yi realizes that the winner will control the spotlight — and decides to try to put her father’s restaurant there instead.
 PapoResumo The essentials in a few seconds Spoilers Seon Jung-won has spent five years developing The Table: K-Chef 2026; the competition was not created after Choi Seung-hyo’s death.
 Kang Han agrees to compete with Song-yi, giving Famiglia the internationally recognized chef it needs to enter the tournament.

 Automatic summary based only on this article. Spoiler warning: this article contains spoilers for Episodes 1 and 2 of Final Table , available on Prime Video. The shift adds an important detail to what Episode 1 revealed about the competition . The Table: K-Chef 2026 was not suddenly created after Choi Seung-hyo’s death. The project already existed, but the crisis gives Pyeongyeon a new reason to push it forward.
 1. The tournament had already been planned for five years
 Seon Jung-won reveals that she has been working on the project for five years because she believes Korean cuisine can take a leading place on the global stage. That detail changes the way Episode 1 reads: the Famiglia crisis did not create the competition. It made the tournament especially useful to the conglomerate.

 2. Pyeongyeon sees the competition as a way out of the Famiglia crisis
 In Episode 1, executives describe the project as their best chance to ease the so-called “Famiglia crisis.” The company wants to launch its new competition while dealing with the fallout from the Choi Seung-hyo case and the possibility of legal action from Song-yi.
 Pyeongyeon directly links the competition to its need to contain the fallout from the Famiglia case. Credit/source: Prime Video reproduction — Final Table , Episode 1. 3. Song-yi realizes what is really at stake
 When Song-yi is invited to enter the tournament, she understands the strategy. Once there is a champion, attention will shift to the winning chef and restaurant. In her eyes, that would also make it easier for the public to move on from Famiglia, her father’s death and the accusations surrounding Pyeongyeon.
 Song-yi realizes that the tournament’s real power lies in deciding who will command the public’s attention after the final. Credit/source: Prime Video reproduction — Final Table , Episode 2. 4. Famiglia can use the same strategy to avoid being forgotten
 Jung-won turns Song-yi’s own argument back on her. A lawsuit against Pyeongyeon could take years, giving the public enough time to forget Choi Seung-hyo and his restaurant. Winning the tournament, however, would immediately put Famiglia back in the spotlight.
 That changes what entering the competition means for Song-yi. It is no longer simply a matter of joining an event organized by the group she holds responsible for her father’s downfall. The tournament becomes a chance to keep Famiglia open and prevent Seung-hyo’s story from disappearing.
 5. Kang Han turns the plan into a real possibility
 There is still one problem: Famiglia needs a chef capable of competing. Episode 2 reveals that the man who saved the restaurant’s dinner service is Chris K., an internationally recognized chef. Song-yi goes after Kang Han before his flight to New York, but he initially has no intention of changing his plans.
 That changes after Song-yi says Pyeongyeon drove her father to his death. Her words trigger a painful memory involving Kang Han’s own father. Shortly afterward, as he is about to leave, he changes direction and agrees to enter the competition with her.
 Kang Han turns away from the departure gate and gives Famiglia the chef it needs to enter the competition. Credit/source: Prime Video reproduction — Final Table , Episode 2. That reversal changes the central conflict of Final Table . Pyeongyeon sees the tournament as a way to move past the crisis; Song-yi decides to enter it precisely to stop Famiglia and her father’s name from being left behind. With Kang Han beside her, that resistance is no longer just an idea.
